says: In next/, a port whose field is a hand-written recursive JSON union (string, number, boolean, null, an array of itself, a record of itself) lists as an agent's tool and takes any JSON there, and no law says whether it should: every node names a type, so the rule that refuses a free JSON field does not see it. The plan's Amendment A-Closed leaves it undecided.
proof: On Node 26.13.0 and effect 4.1.2, a program whose Msg is Schema.Struct({ type: Schema.Literal("put"), held: J }), with J = Schema.suspend(() => Schema.Union([Schema.String, Schema.Finite, Schema.Boolean, Schema.Null, Schema.Array(J), Schema.Record(Schema.String, J)])).annotate({ identifier: "J" }): Tools.list succeeded and the tool's inputSchema held "$defs":{"J":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"number"},{"type":"boolean"},{"type":"null"},{"type":"array","items":{"$ref":"#/$defs/J"}},{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"$ref":"#/$defs/J"}}]}}. Tools.read([program], "probe_put", { value: { held: { any: [1, "x", null, { deep: true }] } } }) answered {"_tag":"write","program":"pack/probe","m":{"type":"put","held":{"any":[1,"x",null,{"deep":true}]}}}. Schema.Json in the same field fails the list with unsupported_schema.
cost: A program can hand an agent an open field by spelling JSON out by hand, which decision 0210's closed schema is meant to rule out; or the refusal of Schema.Json is stricter than it needs to be. Until a person picks, either reading can ship.
